page: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-75s-amd is an entry-level compute-focused instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with two threads per core. Hardware specifications include 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, 32 MB shared L3 cache, and instruction support for AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a bundled 75 GB local NVMe SSD, alongside 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no GPUs attached.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional single-thread performance, with stress-ng single-core processing ranking in the top tier (3422.98) and Geekbench single-core reaching a strong score of 2127.0. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks (256MB) shows strong throughput at 111.47 GB/sec, alongside rapid single-threaded compression and decompression figures. In contrast, parallel throughput scales moderately: multi-core stress-ng (13653.07), PassMark CPU (11667.73), and software compilation on Clang fall within median ranges, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations register lower-tier scores.

Resource allocation presents a specific performance profile tailored to CPU-bound execution rather than scale-out memory access. With a 1:2 ratio of vCPUs to gigabytes of RAM, the voc-c-4c-8gb-75s-amd delivers high computing density per core, but is constrained for large resident working sets. Similarly, static web serving throughput (3.83 GB/sec) and medium-scale LLM inference (12.33 prompt tokens/sec on 7B models) exhibit clear bottlenecks attributable to total core and RAM capacity.

Given its strong per-thread metrics and dedicated core allocation, the instance is best suited for compute-oriented workloads, batch data compression, microservices, application build pipelines, and processing tasks that rely on AVX-512 vector acceleration. It is less suited for heavy database systems or memory-intensive analytical processing.

The instance features a 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio, a bundled 75 GB local NVMe SSD, and 1 included public IPv4 address, without GPU acceleration. CPU capabilities include AVX-512, VAES, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Benchmarks emphasize top-tier single-core performance, evidenced by a 3422.98 stress-ng single-core score and solid Geekbench single-thread results, while multi-core operations and PassMark metrics align with mid-range baselines. Tradeoffs stem from the limited 8.0 GB RAM footprint, which restricts complex databases or large language model inference. The instance is well matched for software compilation, CI/CD runners, single-threaded batch processing, and lightweight compute workloads.
